justifications.functional_suitability: Elements like Admission Management Service, Clinical Workspace, Billing Management Service, and Patient Portal address R-01 through R-04. However, explicit mechanisms for resource clash checking in scheduling are barely specified.
justifications.performance_efficiency: CQRS with dedicated PostgreSQL Read Replicas, Redis caching in Patient Cache Manager, and asynchronous logging via Secure Message Broker directly support the sub-second P95 EMR retrieval target.
justifications.compatibility: The dedicated FHIR Integration Engine (FHIR Router, FHIR Resource Mapper) fully satisfies HL7 FHIR interoperability for External Labs/Imaging. Standard protocols integrate Insurance Payment Gateways and the external Identity Provider.
justifications.usability: Dedicated interfaces serve each user group: Patient Web Frontend for patients, EMR Presentation Component for clinicians, and Billing & Admin Suite for administrative staff. Administrative user interfaces remain slightly generic.
justifications.reliability: While Kafka provides broker durability and replicas support read availability, Core Datastore relies on a single Primary Write Datastore, which fails to provide the true active-active multi-region topology needed for 99.99% uptime.
justifications.security: Security is thoroughly addressed via HSM with FIPS 140-2 AES-256 management, API Gateway MFA/OAuth verification, zero-trust mTLS (SPIFFE/SPIRE), and an immutable WORM Audit Logging Service.
justifications.maintainability: Containers and components are neatly partitioned around domain boundaries (Clinical Workspace, Billing & Admin Suite, FHIR Integration Engine) with clean gRPC/mTLS contracts and CQRS separation.
justifications.portability: Workloads run on Kubernetes across both environments. Using MinIO alongside AWS S3 Object Lock and standard PostgreSQL facilitates consistent deployment across on-prem-k8s and AWS eu-central-1.

PERF-01.justification: CQRS architecture isolates reads onto dedicated PostgreSQL Read Replicas, and Envoy handles high-throughput routing. However, clinical EMR data lacks an in-memory caching layer comparable to the Patient Portal.
sensitivity_points: PostgreSQL read replica query performance under concurrent peak traffic
Absence of a dedicated in-memory cache in the clinical workspace
tradeoffs: Read replica isolation improves latency but introduces eventual consistency latency

PERF-02.justification: CQRS ensures heavy write ingestion to Primary Write Datastore does not degrade Read Replicas serving EMRs. However, the FHIR Integration Engine lacks an explicit durable ingestion queue for backpressure.
sensitivity_points: PostgreSQL primary master write throughput during high-rate ingestion bursts
Backpressure management inside Apache Camel and Node.js components
tradeoffs: Decoupled read/write datastores preserve read performance at the expense of replication lag

AVAIL-01.justification: Core Datastore relies on a single Primary Write Datastore master. The model lacks active-active multi-region replication and automated cross-site failover mechanisms needed for a sub-minute hybrid recovery without data loss.
sensitivity_points: Single primary database master bottleneck in a hybrid cloud deployment
Lack of cross-region active-active database replication and failover orchestration
tradeoffs: Single-primary architecture avoids multi-master write conflicts but impairs disaster recovery times

AVAIL-02.justification: PostgreSQL clustering supports replica promotion, but the architecture specifies no transactional outbox, idempotency tables, or distributed saga handling inside the Billing Management Service to guarantee zero lost or duplicated claims.
sensitivity_points: Database crash detection and leader re-election timing threshold
Deduplication mechanisms for in-flight insurance webhook retries
tradeoffs: Strict write consistency without compensating sagas risks aborted claim transactions during crashes

MOD-01.justification: Clinical workspace and EMR domains remain completely isolated from billing. Modifying the integration requires updates inside Billing Management Service because there is no isolated external clearinghouse adapter component.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between general billing business logic and gateway integration protocols
tradeoffs: Consolidating billing features simplifies service topology but increases internal component modifications

MOD-02.justification: Changes are neatly localized to Admission Management Service, Primary Write Datastore schema, and WORM Audit Logging Service ingestion payload, meeting the requirement of at most three components within one sprint.
sensitivity_points: Extensibility of relational database schemas across CQRS projections
tradeoffs: Structured schemas enforce data integrity but require coordinated projection migrations

SEC-01.justification: API Gateway enforces MFA validation via Security Filter and delegated IdP. Rate Limiter identifies abuse. However, automated real-time security alerting components are not explicitly depicted in the architecture.
sensitivity_points: Strict enforcement of step-up MFA verification at edge ingress filter
Latency of token revocation checks against distributed Redis cluster
tradeoffs: Edge MFA and distributed rate checking increases request processing latency

SEC-02.justification: Clinical Data Orchestrator emits break-glass and read events asynchronously to WORM Audit Logging Service, utilizing Kafka, HSM-backed cryptographic signing, and AWS S3 Object Lock for 10-year immutable retention.
sensitivity_points: Guaranteed emission of read events for every clinical record access
Cryptographic signing integrity backed by hardware security modules
tradeoffs: Auditing every record read increases message bus overhead and storage requirements
